content:
The [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Work out monthly auto loan payments before you buy. Enter your loan amount, interest rate (yearly) and term and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A car loan calculator shows the monthly payment and total interest on an auto loan, so you can negotiate on the full price rather than just the monthly figure. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [EMI Calculator](/emi-calculator).

## How to use the Car Loan Calculator

Start by entering your loan amount, then entering your interest rate (yearly) (%) and finally entering your term (years). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your loan amount.
2. Enter your interest rate (yearly) (%).
3. Enter your term (years).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly rate (annual ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of monthly payments.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Financing 30,000 at 7% over 5 years costs about 594.04 a month and 5,642.31 in total interest. Try the same figures in the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Loan amount: 30000, Interest rate (yearly): 7 %, Term: 5 years), the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) returns Monthly payment: 594.04, Total interest: 5,642.16, Total repaid: 35,642.16, Number of payments: 60. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Get pre-approved by a bank before visiting the dealer.
- Avoid stretching to 72–84 months — cars depreciate faster than you repay.
- Negotiate the vehicle price first, then the financing.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good car loan term?

Many advisers recommend 60 months or less to avoid owing more than the car is worth. Try it with your own numbers in the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Should I include my trade-in?

Yes — subtract your trade-in value and down payment from the price to get the loan amount. Try it with your own numbers in the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Car Loan Calculator use?

M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly rate (annual ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of monthly payments. You can see it in action in the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Car Loan Calculator?

Just Loan amount, Interest rate (yearly) and Term. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

Yes. The Car Loan Calculator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator) and start straight away.
